newsitem.title: USA: CME cattle end up, feeders up but off new highs.
newsitem.headline: CME cattle end up, feeders up but off new highs.

text.p: CME live cattle futures rallied again late and closed at two-month highs, buoyed by a firmer tone to cash cattle which touched off buy stops, traders said.
Feeder cattle futures ended higher but gains were pared after new contract highs were set, traders said.

Live cattle closed 0.775 cent per lb higher to 0.150 lower with August up most at 65.750 cents. Distant April set a new high. Feeder cattle ended 0.400 cent per lb higher to 0.075 lower with August up 0.025 at 81.150 cents after setting a new contract high of 82.000 cents early. All but April and May feeders posted new contract highs on the early runup.

Early resistance in live cattle lacked follow through and prices shot up late as short covering combined with commercial support to touch off chart-based buy stops, floor sources said. A stronger tone in both fed cattle and boxed beef sparked demand, they said.
The futures rally began Wednesday when packers raised bids to $62 as they became short of cattle for near-term needs and boxed beef sales were better than expected.
"Packers are still short cattle up north," said Jim Clarkson, analyst for A and A Inc.
"Packers will likely pay more for cattle next week and feedlots will be asking $64 to $65," another trader added.
Early analysts' estimates on next Friday's total U.S. Cattle Inventory report as of July 1 were ranging from 108.4 million to 109.6 million head, 97 to 98 percent of last year.

Analyst projections on USDA's Cattle-on-Feed report ranged from 114 to 117 percent of a year ago for July 1 on-feed supplies in the seven key cattle feeding states, with June placements ranging from 109 to 125.1 percent of a year ago and June marketings ranging from 101 to 106.9 percent.
RBH and LIT division of First Options continued to buy late while Cargill Investor Services was buying October and selling August, pit sources said.

Feeders surged early to new contract highs on another gain in the CME feeder cattle index, lower corn futures and outlooks for tight feeder supplies. Profit taking developed near midday when corn futures rallied but the runup in live cattle futures again prompted late short covering interest, traders said.
The latest CME feeder cattle index jumped $0.62 per cwt to $81.37, a new high for the move and the highest level in over three years, since April 15, 1994.
Estimates on next week's U.S. Cattle Inventory report point to feeder cattle supplies at 96.4 to 98 percent of last year as of July 1.
Early estimates on the projected 1997 calf crop were 97 to 98 percent.
Boneless beef and beef trimmings futures also rallied late to new highs with trimmings pacing the advance on short covering and new buying following the runup in live cattle futures.
Lind-Waldock bought October and R.J. O'Brien sold while Rosenthal Collins bought October, traders said. Spreaders sold trimmings and bought boneless beef, pit sources said.

Trimmings ended 2.80 to 0.60 cent per lb higher with August up most at 48.00 cents. August through December posted new contract highs. Boneless beef finished unchanged to 1.00 higher with August up 0.50 at 96.00. October and April set new contract highs.
